children: Strong festive demand drove wholesale volumes across India's passenger vehicle (PV) and two-wheeler (2W) segments in October, with both reporting growth ahead of Nomura's estimates. PV wholesales rose 11% year-on-year against the brokerage's estimate of 7%, while two-wheeler volumes increased 15%, compared with its estimate of 12%.In its India Autos October 2026 report dated November 2, Nomura said Maruti Suzuki and Hyundai Motor India reported passenger vehicle wholesales ahead of expectations. Medium and heavy commercial vehicle (MHCV) volumes grew 25%, in line with estimates, while tractor wholesales declined 13%, against the brokerage's expectation of a 7% fall.Dealer feedback suggested healthy festive demand led by EVs, large SUVs and scooters, while hatchbacks lost market share. Early festive trends indicated that Ather Energy and TVS Motor outperformed in two-wheelers, while Royal Enfield and Bajaj Auto underperformed. In passenger vehicles, Mahindra & Mahindra and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles outperformed.Nomura said most automakers were guiding for high-single-digit to low-double-digit growth in the second half of FY27, compared with its earlier expectation of low- to mid-single-digit growth."While near-term demand remains healthy, we remain watchful of the impact of rising inflation, interest rates and oil prices," the brokerage said.It also noted that EV adoption was gaining traction, with OEMs having established EV portfolios better positioned to gain market share over the long term. "We believe the industry is approaching an important inflection point, with EV penetration continuing to increase across PVs and 2Ws," it said.PV wholesales stood at 519,000 units, while two-wheeler volumes were 2.55 million units. Retail volumes, however, declined 15% and 28%, respectively.Maruti Suzuki's overall volumes rose 25% to 276,000 units, while Hyundai's domestic sales increased 17% to 62,800 units. Tata Motors' domestic PV sales grew 21% to 73,900 units.Nomura said commodity pressure persisted in the third quarter, although most automakers expected margins to remain stable sequentially, supported by pricing actions. It continues to prefer Mahindra & Mahindra, Hyundai Motor India, Tata Motors Commercial Vehicles, TVS Motor and Sona BLW Precision Forgings.

title: Nomura sees strong festive demand lifting auto volumes in October; PVs, 2Ws beat estimates
